clue.text: Scotch —- an acceptable term for European?

indicators.note: read as accept-able, able to take something in, so the ruin word takes in another piece

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to dish it, ruin its chances
taken as written

explanation.surface: A query about whether a word for a Scot can fairly be applied to Europeans generally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' tempts you towards Scotland, but here it is a verb meaning to scupper, DISH. 'Acceptable' is the containment signal: DISH accepts AN to give D-AN-ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish names the people, language and things of Denmark, a European nation, hence a term for one sort of European.

clue.text: In time, he's to be put up and dry out — do just that

indicators.note: the following pieces go inside the word for a point in time

parts.note: a date is a fixed time

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means reading upwards, so the pronoun is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

indicators.note: out signals the letters of dry are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A drinker told to sober up and dry out, timed and supervised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be put up' reverses HE to EH; 'out' rearranges DRY to YDR; 'In' sets both inside DATE: D-EH-YDR-ATE. 'Do just that' refers back to drying out.
explanation.definitionFit: To dehydrate is to remove the water from something, which is exactly what drying out does.

clue.text: First three oddly disqualified, announce what you may call a one-off

definitions.text: what you may call a one-off

indicators.note: the first three letters in odd positions, the first, third and fifth, are struck out of the word announce

explanation.surface: A competition where three early entrants are oddly ruled out and a single event is declared.
explanation.walkthrough: ANNOUNCE loses its 1st, 3rd and 5th letters, A, N and U, leaving NONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonce word is coined for a single occasion, so nonce describes something used just once.

clue.text: Starts to soothe emergency case? It does, typically.

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two following words are taken

parts.note: the dative is a grammatical case, used for the indirect object

explanation.surface: A medical emergency in which a patient is calmed, with a remark that this usually works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It does, typically' refers back to soothing: a sedative typically soothes. 'Case' looks medical but is grammatical.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a drug whose usual job is to calm a patient, so it is the thing that soothes.

clue.text: With least amount put in bid, finally going very pale

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, so the clue's smallest amount goes into the shortened bid
the last letter of the word for a bid departs

parts.note: an offer is a bid
a whit is the smallest amount, as in 'not a whit'

explanation.surface: An auction where someone raises by the smallest increment while turning pale with nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally going' removes the R at the end of OFFER, leaving OFFE; 'put in' sets WHIT inside it: OFF-WHIT-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-white is a very pale shade, white with a faint tint of grey or yellow.

clue.text: Begin to make sense, and line up best-quality material

parts.note: soldiers ordered to fall in line up in ranks
top means best, as in top quality
lace is a delicate openwork fabric

explanation.surface: A tailor matching up the finest fabric so everything starts to make sense.
explanation.definitionFit: When facts fall into place, they come together so that the situation becomes clear and understandable.

clue.text: Squirm — rebuke cut 'short delight

parts.note: to wig someone is an old informal word for to scold

indicators.note: the word for delight loses its last letter

parts.note: glee is delight

explanation.surface: Someone wriggling when a scolding cuts their pleasure short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' takes the last E off GLEE to give GLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wiggle is to move with quick twisting motions, which is how one squirms.

clue.text: Coining alias, to appear unidentifiable

indicators.note: an alias is an assumed name, so these letters take on a different form

explanation.surface: A forger dreaming up a false name so as to go unrecognised.
explanation.walkthrough: COINING rearranged gives INCOGNI, followed by TO; 'appear' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incognito has a concealed identity, so they cannot be identified.

clue.text: Start of chapter in story built up to brilliant effect

indicators.note: the opening letter is placed inside the turned-round story
in a down clue, built up means written from the bottom upward, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A novel whose first chapter builds up towards a dazzling climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Built up' turns TALE into ELAT; 'in' puts C inside it: E-C-LAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat means conspicuous brilliance of success or effect, borrowed from the French word for burst.

clue.text: Dejected, having to put up with object of devotion's rejection

parts.note: to hang a picture is to put it up; 'with' joins the next piece

indicators.note: rejection turns the object of devotion back on itself, so its word is read backwards

parts.note: God is the object of religious devotion

explanation.surface: Someone downcast after their idol has spurned them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejection' turns GOD round to DOG, which follows HANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is shamefaced and miserable, so the adjective means dejected.

clue.text: Make more money from act as a tease, successfully

definitions.meaning: obtain a pay increase from an employer
provoke a reaction from someone by teasing

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom literally suggests securing a pay increase, and figuratively means managing to provoke a reaction by teasing.

clue.text: Suggesting reason for what follows

definitions.meaning: describing the natural next step, the one that follows as a consequence

explanation.walkthrough: The printed line break splits 'follows' as 'fol-lows'. The adjective serves both senses: rational thinking, and the obvious consequence, as in 'the next step'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both rational in argument and naturally consequent, as in the sensible next step that follows.

clue.text: Lived with daughter wanting leather trimming

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees
a welt is a strip of leather sewn round the edge of a shoe upper

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's life story: she lived with her daughter, who was always short of leather edging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' and 'wanting' (needing) merely link D and WELT.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, to reside, so it means lived somewhere.

clue.text: Mean to include everything I. put in — followers'll see it

indicators.note: the stingy word takes in the following pieces

parts.note: tight means mean with money

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the word for everything

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A miser grudgingly agreeing to include everything he had contributed, in full view of his disciples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in' sets I inside ALL to make AILL; 'to include' puts that inside TIGHT: T-AILL-IGHT. The drivers behind a car are its followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail light is the red lamp at the back of a vehicle, the one seen by traffic following behind.

clue.text: Solemnly declare fool always was simply a consumer

parts.note: an ass is a fool
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
someone who ate merely consumed food

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on someone: a perpetual fool who only ever consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: To asseverate is a formal word meaning to declare or affirm something earnestly.

clue.text: About to introduce girl dressed in black, worth looking over!

indicators.note: the outer word clothes the inner pieces

parts.note: sable is the heraldic name for black

indicators.note: the first piece comes before and introduces the girl

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl dressed in black being introduced, and well worth a look.
explanation.walkthrough: C followed by ANN goes inside SABLE: S-CANN-ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scannable can be scanned, looked over quickly or examined.

clue.text: Branch in state of neglect nothing's left

indicators.note: 'nothing's left' says the nothing has departed from the word for neglect

parts.note: limbo is a state of being forgotten or neglected
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A tree branch in a neglected garden where nothing else remains.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O away from LIMBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a large branch of a tree, as in 'out on a limb'.

clue.text: Date woman may hope to become union member

definitions.text: Date woman may hope to become union member

parts.words: Date woman may hope to become union member
parts.note: a man a woman is going out with, whom she may hope to marry; the union is marriage, not a trade union

explanation.walkthrough: 'Union member' suggests a trade unionist, but the union is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A boyfriend is a regular male companion one dates, and may become a husband, a partner in the union of marriage.

clue.text: With' support of opera house, set up on location in Hawaii

indicators.note: in a down entry the opera is placed underneath, holding up the rest
in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Lulu is Alban Berg's opera

explanation.surface: An opera house built on a site in Hawaii, with backing secured.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry LULU sits below HO + NO, supporting them.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the capital city of Hawaii, on the island of Oahu.

clue.text: Test of English provided by. Times in the morning?

parts.note: x is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'
a.m. marks the hours before noon

explanation.surface: Asking whether a morning English paper's crossword is a test of the language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign, X; 'provided by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a test of knowledge, short for examination.

clue.text: Shy people mostly go off pollster's study

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so the letters are jumbled
the word people loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Bashful folk tend to avoid an opinion researcher's survey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims PEOPLE to PEOPL; 'off' shuffles SHY + PEOPL + GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Psephology is the statistical study of elections and voting, which is the pollster's field.

clue.text: Adorn cot, perhaps, and check child out

parts.note: a cot is one kind of bed

indicators.note: the abbreviation for child goes out of the word check

explanation.surface: A parent decorating a cot and checking that the baby is out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: CHECK without CH leaves ECK.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedeck is to decorate or adorn lavishly.

clue.text: Notes breaks in flow of motorway, in a state

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are set into the stream of the following pieces

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: the word notes is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Musical notes interrupted by the roar of motorway traffic, leaving someone flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks' jumbles NOTES to NESOT; 'in flow of' sets it inside M + IN + A: MIN-NESOT-A. 'In a state' looks like agitation, but 'state' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the states of the USA, in the upper Midwest.

clue.text: Notes type of key used to open such bars

definitions.text: type of key used to open such bars
definitions.meaning: a key signature stands at the start of a stave's bars, so this kind of key opens them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' and 'bars' suggest a lock and prison, but the key is a musical key and the bars are measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Music means notes written or played, and a musical key signature opens the bars of a score.

clue.text: Getting on with senior?

definitions.meaning: higher in age than another person

explanation.walkthrough: 'With' links two senses of the comparative of 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of old suits both someone getting on in years and someone senior to another.

clue.text: Romeo featured in silly sketch, perhaps

indicators.note: the letter appears inside the word for silly

parts.note: daft means silly
Romeo is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for R

explanation.surface: A comedy sketch in which Romeo appears as a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside DAFT: D-R-AFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version, of which a sketch is one example.

clue.text: Put down topic for study

definitions.meaning: to bring under control or subdue
a school or university discipline, such as history

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to subdue or put down; as a noun it is a discipline studied at school.

clue.text: Bring up teaching style

parts.note: read as a request to raise a child in a teaching manner, that is to instruct and train them

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a request to raise the matter of teaching method, but it describes rearing a child through instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To educate is to bring up or rear a child by teaching and training.

clue.text: Mark, having dealt with playwright, given audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the playwright's name is to be heard said aloud

parts.note: Anton Chekhov was the Russian dramatist who wrote The Cherry Orchard

explanation.surface: An actor scores well after tackling a Chekhov piece at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a score, but with 'having dealt with' it describes ticking items off a list.
explanation.definitionFit: To check off is to tick an item on a list once it has been dealt with.

clue.text: Given citation, turned out to put in 'declaration of proof

indicators.note: the rearranged short word is put inside the abbreviation

parts.note: QED, quod erat demonstrandum, ends a proof

indicators.note: the letters of out are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: Being cited, a statement turned out to be inserted to show something was proved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' rearranges OUT to UOT; 'to put in' places that inside QED: Q-UOT-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be quoted is to be cited, given a citation by someone repeating your words.
